{
  "problem": "Design a minimal REST API for task management.",
  "objectives": [
    "Create an API that allows clients to create, read, update, and delete tasks.",
    "Ensure the API follows RESTful conventions.",
    "Keep the design simple and minimal."
  ],
  "deliverables": [
    "A JSON document specifying the API endpoints, including HTTP methods, paths, request/response schemas, and example payloads."
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "The API must be RESTful.",
    "The API should be minimal, focusing only on core task management functionality."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The API will use JSON for request and response bodies.",
    "Task objects will have fields: id (string or number), title (string), description (string, optional), status (string, default 'pending').",
    "The API will store tasks in-memory, with no persistence.",
    "Standard HTTP status codes will be used (201 for creation, 200 for updates/retrieval, 204 for deletion, 404 for not found).",
    "No authentication or authorization is required.",
    "The API will be self-contained and not depend on external services."
  ],
  "non_goals": [
    "Include authentication or authorization mechanisms.",
    "Implement pagination, filtering, or sorting for task listing.",
    "Support advanced features like task assignments, due dates, or categories unless explicitly required."
  ],
  "acceptance": [
    "The API design includes endpoints: POST /tasks, GET /tasks, GET /tasks/{id}, PUT /tasks/{id}, DELETE /tasks/{id}.",
    "The design specifies the request and response formats for each endpoint.",
    "The design follows REST conventions (e.g., resource naming, statelessness, proper use of HTTP methods).",
    "The design document is provided in JSON format as specified."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "Without pagination, the GET /tasks endpoint could return a large number of tasks, causing performance issues.",
    "In-memory storage means tasks are lost when the server restarts, reducing reliability.",
    "Lack of authentication exposes the API to unauthorized access and data manipulation.",
    "Ambiguity in the task schema could lead to inconsistencies between client and server."
  ]
}
